T04_class_distribution.caption: Class distribution of the binary target (At-Risk = LastTermPercentage ≤ 50%).

S01_data_audit.caption: Variable-level audit of the primary dataset (before cleaning).
S01_data_audit.note: DifficultSubject has missing responses; these are coded as an explicit 'Unknown' level.

S02_descriptives_by_class.caption: Descriptive statistics of the 13 predictors by outcome class.
S02_descriptives_by_class.note: Continuous / Likert: Mann–Whitney U with rank-biserial r. Categorical: χ² (Fisher exact for sparse 2×2) with Cramér's V.

S03_vif.caption: Variance inflation factors of the 13 predictors.
S03_vif.note: All VIF < 5 indicates no problematic multicollinearity.

T05_smote_distribution.caption: Class distribution of the training partition before and after SMOTE-NC.
T05_smote_distribution.note: Held-out test set (n = 363, 20 At-Risk) is never resampled. Inside cross-validation SMOTE-NC is re-fitted on each training fold only. Primary analysis uses: No resampling (justified in Table S5); SMOTE-NC is a sensitivity analysis.

S04_hyperparameters.caption: Hyper-parameters selected by stratified 10-fold GridSearchCV on the training partition.
S04_hyperparameters.note: Optimisation criterion: average_precision (PR-AUC), appropriate for a 5.5% minority class.

T06_model_comparison.caption: Model comparison: stratified 10-fold CV on the training partition (mean ± SD) and held-out test performance with stratified bootstrap 95% CIs.
T06_model_comparison.note: CV columns: 10 folds of the training partition (n = 845). Test columns: n = 363 (20 At-Risk), 2000 stratified bootstrap replicates, percentile intervals. Threshold = 0.5.

T07_classwise.caption: Class-wise precision, recall and F1 for both classes.
T07_classwise.note: '(%)' columns: mean ± SD over 10 CV folds of the training partition. 'Test' columns: single evaluation on the held-out set; support = number of test students per class.

T08_lr_vs_xgb.caption: Logistic Regression vs XGBoost on 10-fold CV scores: Welch's t-test and the Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t-test.
T08_lr_vs_xgb.note: CV folds share training data, so Welch's t-test (which assumes independence) is anti-conservative; the corrected resampled t-test should be used for inference.

T09_kappa_brier.caption: Reliability of the six classifiers: Cohen's κ, MCC and Brier score on the held-out test set.
T09_kappa_brier.note: Agreement levels follow Landis & Koch (1977). Brier skill score > 0 means better than always predicting the base rate.

A01_mcnemar.caption: Pairwise McNemar tests on hold-out hard predictions.
A01_mcnemar.note: Exact binomial test when b + c < 25, otherwise continuity-corrected χ². p-values adjusted for 15 comparisons with Benjamini–Hochberg.

A02_friedman.caption: Friedman test on fold-wise accuracy ranks (10 folds, six models).
A02_friedman.note: Models whose mean ranks differ by more than the critical difference (CD) differ significantly (Nemenyi post-hoc).

A03_delong.caption: Pairwise DeLong tests of hold-out ROC-AUC.

S06_global_importance.caption: Global feature importance of the final model: mean |SHAP|, permutation importance and standardised coefficients.
S06_global_importance.note: Spearman ρ(SHAP, PFI) = 0.747; ρ(SHAP, |std. coef|) = 0.962. PFI: mean drop in test ROC-AUC over permutations. Odds ratios: per +1 SD increase (binary/ordinal features: per SD of their code); nominal features: one OR per one-hot level vs. the intercept.

T10_shap_stability.caption: Rank stability of global SHAP importance across 10 random seeds (re-split + re-fit).

A04_shap_stability_matrix.caption: Pairwise Spearman correlations of global SHAP rankings across 10 seeds.

A05_shap_lime_instances.caption: Instance-level SHAP–LIME agreement (50 test students: all true At-Risk + random Not At-Risk).
A05_shap_lime_instances.note: τ computed over all 13 features on absolute attributions. Sign agreement: share of SHAP top-5 features where LIME weight has the same sign (LIME weights are on the probability scale, SHAP on log-odds).

T11_shap_lime_agreement.caption: SHAP–LIME rank agreement (50 test students, stratified).

T01_prex_dimensions.caption: Theoretical grounding of the PREX-Edu pedagogical dimensions.
T01_prex_dimensions.note: Socio-demographic features (age, gender, parent education, income, study space, extracurricular, difficult subject) are retained in the model but form a separate, non-actionable context block.

T12_faithfulness_ablation.caption: Faithfulness ablation: performance drop when features are removed in PREX-Edu order vs random order.
T12_faithfulness_ablation.note: Removal = replacement by the training mean (numeric) or mode (categorical). Baseline on the test set (n = 363): ROC-AUC = 0.9832, accuracy = 0.9697. Random: 100 random orders. Area under the degradation curve (ROC-AUC): PREX = 0.5727, SHAP order = 0.5595, random = 0.8118 (lower = more faithful). Accuracy is reported for continuity but is uninformative at 5.5% prevalence; ROC-AUC is the primary faithfulness metric.

S07_instance_aopc.caption: Instance-level faithfulness: area over the perturbation curve (AOPC) for students flagged At-Risk.
S07_instance_aopc.note: Flagged = P(At-Risk) ≥ 0.339 (F1-optimal threshold from training-set CV). AOPC@6 = mean drop in P(At-Risk) over the first six removals; higher = removed features mattered more. Wilcoxon PREX vs random: W = 0.0, p = 9.54e-07; PREX vs SHAP: W = 51.0, p = 0.024. SHAP order is the per-instance upper bound; PREX-Edu constrains removal to whole dimensions.

S08_dimension_ablation.caption: Dimension-level ablation: does the R_k ranking predict the performance cost of removing a dimension?
S08_dimension_ablation.note: R_k = sum of |SHAP| (operator set in config). Spearman ρ(mean R_k, ΔROC-AUC) = 0.800. Context block shown for completeness.

A06a_aggregation_summary.caption: Sensitivity of dimension rankings to the aggregation operator: sum vs cardinality-normalised mean.

A06b_dimension_scores.caption: Mean dimension scores under sum and cardinality-normalised (mean) aggregation.

A08_per_student_prex.caption: Per-student PREX-Edu risk magnitudes for the 10 flagged test students with the highest predicted risk.
A08_per_student_prex.note: Student ID = row number in the original dataset. Margin = dominant minus second-ranked R_k; a larger margin indicates a clearer single intervention target.

S09_dominant_distribution.caption: Distribution of the dominant PREX-Edu dimension and attribution coverage.
S09_dominant_distribution.note: Coverage = share of a student's total |SHAP| captured by the four actionable dimensions; the remainder belongs to non-actionable context features.

T13_demographic_parity.caption: Demographic parity of At-Risk predictions by gender and family income (hold-out test set).
T13_demographic_parity.note: P(ŷ=1 | group) is the share of the subgroup flagged At-Risk (threshold 0.339, F1-optimal on training CV). Disparate-impact ratio < 0.8 or > 1.25 would breach the four-fifths rule. With ≤ 20 true At-Risk students in the test set, subgroup TPRs are highly uncertain; see script 14 for the full-sample audit with CIs.

A07a_shap_by_gender.caption: Mean absolute SHAP value of the six most important features by gender.
A07a_shap_by_gender.note: Last row: Kruskal–Wallis test of equal |SHAP| distributions across subgroups (no multiplicity correction).

A07b_shap_by_income.caption: Mean absolute SHAP value of the six most important features by income range.
A07b_shap_by_income.note: Last row: Kruskal–Wallis test of equal |SHAP| distributions across subgroups (no multiplicity correction).

S10_prex_by_subgroup.caption: Distribution of the dominant PREX-Edu dimension by demographic subgroup (test set).
S10_prex_by_subgroup.note: χ² test of independence between subgroup and dominant dimension. Non-significant p indicates that the pedagogical explanation a teacher receives does not systematically depend on the student's demographics.

S12_intervention_per_student.caption: Simulated intervention effect per dimension for each flagged At-Risk test student.
S12_intervention_per_student.note: ΔP = reduction in predicted At-Risk probability after improving only that dimension's features.

S11_intervention_simulation.caption: Intervention simulation: does acting on the top-ranked PREX-Edu dimension produce the largest risk reduction?
S11_intervention_simulation.note: Full dose: each feature of the targeted dimension improves by 1 SD, so two-feature dimensions receive twice the total effort. Equal budget: every dimension receives the same total effort (1 SD-unit split across its features). Ranks 1–4 and the random comparison use the PREX-Edu operator set in config. This is a computational coherence check, not a causal estimate.

S13_counterfactual_summary.caption: Actionable counterfactual explanations for flagged At-Risk students (greedy minimal-cost search).
S13_counterfactual_summary.note: Target: P(At-Risk) below the decision threshold 0.339. Only the six actionable features may change; demographics are immutable. Step sizes: 0.25 SD for continuous features, 1 point for Likert items, Yes for attendance. Cost = sum of standardised step sizes.

S14_counterfactual_examples.caption: Counterfactual examples (first 10 flagged At-Risk test students).
S14_counterfactual_examples.note: Δ columns: change required in each actionable feature to bring predicted risk below 0.339.

S05_imbalance_strategies.caption: Comparison of class-imbalance strategies (5×10 repeated stratified CV, all 1,208 students).
S05_imbalance_strategies.note: Resamplers are fitted inside each training fold only. Threshold = 0.5. ECE = expected calibration error on pooled out-of-fold probabilities (10 quantile bins), mean ± SD over repeats. Ranking metrics (ROC/PR-AUC) are threshold-free; recall/F1 depend on the 0.5 threshold.

S15_power_wilcoxon.caption: Monte-Carlo power of the paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (α = .05, two-sided) on 1–5 Likert ratings.
S15_power_wilcoxon.note: Minimum pairs for 80% power: d_z=0.4: 80; d_z=0.5: 40; d_z=0.6: 30; d_z=0.8: 20. 2000 simulations per cell.

S16_power_designs.caption: Power of candidate replication designs when ratings are clustered within raters (ICC = 0.2).
S16_power_designs.note: The 3 × 5 pilot had ≈ 41% power for a medium effect (d_z = 0.5); ≥ 10 raters × 10 profiles gives ≥ 80% power for d_z = 0.4.

T02_shap_lime_vs_prex.caption: Criterion-based comparison of SHAP/LIME and PREX-Edu.

S17_xai_rubric.caption: Literature-based rubric scores (0–10) underlying Figure 2.
S17_xai_rubric.note: Composite = arithmetic mean of the six dimensions (Eq. 4).

S18_synthetic_fidelity_privacy.caption: Fidelity, privacy and utility of synthetic data generated from the training partition.
S18_synthetic_fidelity_privacy.note: Generators fitted per class on the hold-out training partition (n = 845). Fidelity: SDMetrics quality scores (1 = perfect), mean absolute difference of Spearman correlation matrices, and a 5-fold XGBoost discriminator (AUC 0.5 = synthetic indistinguishable from real). Privacy: Gower distance to the closest real training record (DCR); reference = real hold-out students (5th percentile = 0.0462). A synthetic set is privacy-safe when its DCR distribution is not shifted below the reference. Utility: train on synthetic, test on real (TSTR) vs train-real-test-real ROC-AUC = 0.9669. SMOTE-NC row refers to its interpolated minority records only.

S19_augmentation_utility.caption: Does synthetic augmentation improve At-Risk detection? (2×5-fold repeated CV, evaluation on real students only)
S19_augmentation_utility.note: Generators are fitted on the training fold only; synthetic rows never enter a test fold. Δ = mean paired difference vs real-data-only training; p from the Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t-test.

S24_aggregation_operators.caption: Empirical comparison of SHAP-to-dimension aggregation operators against three model-based ground truths.
S24_aggregation_operators.note: Students = test students flagged At-Risk by the final model (p ≥ 0.339). G1: exact baseline Shapley value of each dimension treated as a single player (5 players incl. context; 32 coalitions; log-odds; reference = training mean/mode). G2: change in log-odds when the dimension is reset to the reference. G3: reduction in P(At-Risk) for an equal 1-SD-unit improvement budget per dimension. The operator with the highest agreement should be adopted as the PREX-Edu aggregation rule (or reported as a sensitivity analysis).

S26_threshold_sensitivity.caption: Sensitivity of discrimination and explanations to the At-Risk threshold τ.
S26_threshold_sensitivity.note: 5×10 repeated stratified CV (hyper-parameters fixed at the τ = 50 selection). PR-AUC lift = PR-AUC / prevalence (random classifier = 1). Explanations from the hold-out LR model at each τ.

S25_crossmodel_prex.caption: Robustness of PREX-Edu explanations to the choice of predictive model.
S25_crossmodel_prex.note: Same 363 test students. High agreement means the pedagogical message does not hinge on the classifier.

A09_survey_instrument.caption: Educator survey instrument (administered per profile and format).
A09_survey_instrument.note: Blinded within-subjects design: each educator rates every profile in both formats (raw SHAP, PREX-Edu) in a randomised order; consent obtained; responses anonymous.

P01_nested_cv_performance.caption: Primary evaluation: nested 10×10-fold repeated stratified cross-validation on all 1208 students (66 At-Risk).
P01_nested_cv_performance.note: 'mean ± SD' over 100 outer test folds. 'pooled [95% CI]': metric on the per-student out-of-fold probability averaged over repeats (n = 1208), stratified bootstrap (2000 replicates). Hyper-parameters tuned by inner 5-fold GridSearchCV (PR-AUC); tuned threshold maximises F1 on inner out-of-fold predictions. Imbalance handling: No resampling inside training folds only.

P02_nested_cv_classwise.caption: Class-wise performance under nested repeated cross-validation.
P02_nested_cv_classwise.note: Mean ± SD over outer folds. Support = number of students of that class, each scored once per repeat.

P03_corrected_ttests.caption: Pairwise model comparison with the Nadeau–Bengio corrected repeated-CV t-test.
P03_corrected_ttests.note: Corrects for the overlap of training sets across CV folds (variance inflated by 1/J + n_test/n_train). Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment within each metric (15 comparisons).

P04_friedman_nemenyi.caption: Friedman test with Nemenyi post-hoc over 100 outer folds.

P05_delong_oof.caption: DeLong tests on per-student out-of-fold probabilities (n = 1208).

P06_mcnemar_oof.caption: McNemar tests on per-student out-of-fold predictions (n = 1208, threshold 0.5).

P07_param_frequency.caption: Most frequently selected hyper-parameters across outer folds (top 3 per model).

S20_calibration.caption: Calibration of out-of-fold predicted probabilities (nested repeated CV, n = 1,208).
S20_calibration.note: Slope < 1 indicates over-confident (too extreme) probabilities; intercept ≠ 0 indicates systematic over/under-estimation (calibration-in-the-large).

S21_operating_points.caption: Operating points: thresholds needed to reach target sensitivity, and the resulting workload.
S21_operating_points.note: Computed on out-of-fold probabilities for all 1,208 students (66 At-Risk). 'Flagged per true At-Risk' is the number of students a school must follow up per correctly identified At-Risk student. Note these thresholds are chosen post hoc on the pooled OOF predictions — use for planning, not as unbiased estimates.

S22_fairness_subgroups.caption: Subgroup performance of the final model on out-of-fold predictions for all 1208 students.
S22_fairness_subgroups.note: Threshold = 0.378 (median inner-CV F1-optimal threshold). Values: point estimate [stratified bootstrap 95% CI, 2000 replicates]. Calibration-in-the-large = mean predicted − observed prevalence.

S23_fairness_gaps.caption: Fairness gaps relative to the reference subgroup (first level of each attribute).
S23_fairness_gaps.note: * = 95% CI excludes 0. Disparate-impact ratio outside [0.8, 1.25] breaches the four-fifths rule. Small subgroups (e.g., 'Prefer not to say', n = 54) produce wide intervals; absence of significance is not evidence of fairness.
